thread.title: COLUMN: Bryce Lindsay is the Lamar Wilkerson of Luke Goodes
thread.title_full: COLUMN: Bryce Lindsay is the Lamar Wilkerson of Luke Goodes

author: Nathan Shriberg
title: COLUMN: Bryce Lindsay is the Lamar Wilkerson of Luke Goodes
text:
Allow me to explain.
Not all guards are created equal. Some are multitalented two-way players who can knock down long-range jumpers and create their own shots. Others are Khristian Lander. Most fall somewhere in between.
Within the guard position, there exists a subcategory: bench scorers.
Every great team has a guard stashed away on the bench who can come in and light up the scoreboard. A sparkplug who can ignite a run and turn a game around in an instant. They play fast and demand the attention of opposing defenses.
Despite coming off the bench, they're frequently a top five player on the roster. At the very least, they're a Luke Goode — a pure shooter.
For Indiana men's basketball, the role has taken many forms in recent years. Two of them were inside Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall on Thursday night.
While Goode watched from the stands, Bryce Lindsay burst onto Branch McCracken Court. In the Hoosiers' 92-69 victory over Bellarmine University, the 6-foot-4 senior guard poured in 15 points off the bench.
The performance was nothing new for Lindsay. He came off the bench in each of Indiana's three preseason exhibitions and led the Hoosiers in scoring twice. Lindsay also notched 14 points in the Hoosiers' regular season-opener against Eastern Illinois University.
Lindsay’s ability to transcend the traditional bounds of a bench scorer makes him special. He isn't expected to breeze by defenders and pull it from 30 feet. Yet, he routinely does both with elegance.
He's a threat from anywhere on the floor. Does that remind you of a certain former Hoosier guard from Ashdown, Arkansas?
Now, let’s slow down for a second and make it absolutely clear that Lamar Wilkerson is a much better player than Lindsay. But if there was a Wilkerson of the role that Goode occupied, it would be Lindsay.
Whether it makes sense or not, it certainly feels right.
Lindsay's performance Thursday wasn't his finest, shooting only 3 for 10 from beyond the arc. However, by the time the final buzzer sounded, Lindsay was the team's second-leading scorer with 15 points.
It's a spot he's accustomed to, having finished as a top two scorer for the Hoosiers in four straight games, exhibitions included.
Goode reached double figures 14 times in his lone season in Bloomington. He began 2024-25 as a benchwarmer, but 11 of the double-digit scoring games came as a starter.
Meanwhile, Lindsay's already done it twice in just two regular season games, both off the bench. Goode made 62 3-pointers in 32 games. Lindsay is on pace for 96, even with his output dropping from preseason play. As such, I think it's fair to bump him out of the Goode tier.
So, what about Wilkerson?
Lindsay won't touch Wilkerson's 20.9 points per game. Rather, prowess from beyond the arc is the most meaningful trait the two share. Combining the preseason and the first two games of the regular season, Lindsay has averaged more than three longballs per game. Last season, Wilkerson became the first Hoosier to hit that mark since James Blackmon in 2016-17.
Unlike Wilkerson, Lindsay has a lot of help. Junior guard Darren Harris and freshman forward Trevor Manhertz each drained multiple 3-pointers against Bellarmine.
"I think it's going to make us really hard to beat," Harris said postgame. "Let alone like two or three of us get going at the same time."
As much as comparing Lindsay to Wilkerson is a stretch, it emphasizes the impact he's had on the Hoosiers even early on. If he remains a consistent scoring threat, maybe Indiana fans will eventually remember him as fondly as Wilkerson, even if he never reaches the same individual highs.
As for the rest of the team?
Maybe Manhertz is the Nick Dorn of Bryson Tuckers and Harris is the Mackenzie Mgbako of Myles Rices. I'll admit those made much less sense. All I know is Sam Alexis is still Sam Alexis. And Indiana is 2-0.
